chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (the first) (peace be upon him) who said:
Four [acts] are from obsession (waswas): eating clay, breaking up clay, clipping the nails with the teeth, and eating the beard.
ai.seo_question: What are the four signs of obsession (waswas) mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq attributes these four specific physical habits—eating clay, breaking up clay, biting nails, and chewing the beard—to *waswas* (obsession or compulsive behavior), linking them to a spiritual or psychological affliction. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing minor physical compulsions as indicators of deeper internal states, often associated with the influence of jinn or excessive attachment to the self. The hadith serves as a practical guide for self-purification (*tazkiyah*) by identifying and correcting these seemingly trivial but spiritually significant behaviors.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-46 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dihqan, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor al-Vaseti, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor al-Vaseti, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, on the authority of Abil Hassan - the first (MGB) ,
“The following four acts are due to obsession: eating clay, breaking up clay, biting one’s nails, and chewing one’s beard (Trichotillomania).”
